_: Spell tiers (module 76 §123). Elemental damage bypasses physical armour and is met by resistances instead — this is what keeps a magic build on the same multiplier stack as a weapon build all game.

healing._: Restoration heals on the same magnitude band; slow enough that it is a between-exchange move, not a mid-combo one.

enchanting._bannedNote: the crafting inputs are banned as crafting inputs only - all crafting reads BASE values, so these effects may still exist for combat use

constantEffectSoulByMagnitude._: Cheap constant effects should be attainable; only big ones need a great soul.

alchemy._: Morrowind's shape with base-stat inputs only: strength = (effAlchemy + Int/10) * apparatus / (3 * effectBaseCost). Restore Health base cost 5.

_tierNote: damage retuned down 2026-08-29 by the sim: at the original values a novice mage out-burst a melee character 3:1 in the low bands. Magic stays the burst archetype, bounded by magicka rather than by damage.
_costReductionNote: Raised from 0.5 to 0.75 (owner, round 2): rare, hard-won gear should have a genuinely strong effect. 75 % still leaves every spell costing something, so no infinite-cast loop exists.

castability._: Morrowind's cast formula as a gate (module 76 §123). Canon's chance is 2 x skill + Willpower/5 - cost; at chance 0 the spell effectively never works and at 50 it is a coin-flip, so the honest 'you can rely on this' line is 50 points inside canon's boundary - which is also what actually matches the spells a Morrowind character of that skill carries.
castability._workingFraction: a caster does not lead with the biggest spell they can reliably hold. 0.6 puts a starting mage on a ~19-damage spell and an endgame one on ~100 before magnitude and gear - which is where Morrowind's own starting and master spellbooks actually sit, and it keeps the levelling pace honest: a cast is worth one use point however big it is, so a mage who one-shots everything levels Destruction slowly.
